comments.text: Making the create `IF NOT EXISTS` hides the root cause instead of fixing it. Since the leftover index is still never dropped, any change to such an index's definition (different columns, adding/removing UNIQUE, a WHERE clause) is now silently ignored: the old index stays and the new definition is skipped with no error, so e.g. a newly requested UNIQUE constraint is never enforced while the collection schema claims it is. It would also silently skip creating an index whose name collides with an index on another table. Fix dropCollectionIndexes instead: set the parsed TableName to the collection's (old) name before the IsValid() check (as createCollectionIndexes already does) so indexes persisted without a table name are dropped and recreated normally. Please add a regression test with an index stored without a table name whose definition is then changed.
